title: fix(metadata-protocol): a /meta object read serves the effective runtime schema, whichever layer answered (#6562)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#6562

Implements the maintainer's ruling of record (2026-08-08 11:59Z) — **Option B: the `/meta` object read serves the EFFECTIVE runtime schema**, and the overlay-backed minority path converges on the registry-backed majority.

## The defect, re-measured on `origin/main` before any edit

The issue body is a lead, so its premise was verified first. Both halves confirmed, one detail corrected.

A registry-backed `GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name` for an object whose author declared exactly one field (`amount`):

```
field names: [amount, created_at, created_by, organization_id,
              owner_id, owning_business_unit_id, updated_at, updated_by]
```

The same authored body served from a `sys_metadata` overlay row: `[amount]`. Nothing in either response says which link answered.

**Correction to the issue's `multiTenant` note.** The card says "`organization_id` is conditional per `applySystemFields`'s options". Measured in both modes, the column always EXISTS; `multiTenant` changes only whether it is `indexed`. That matches `resolveInjectedSystemColumns`' own header ("the `multiTenant` option changes only whether `organization_id` is INDEXED, never whether it exists"), and it is why nothing in the read path takes a `multiTenant` input. Both modes are pinned anyway.

## What changed

`governServedItem` — the per-exit seam #4513 already established — now composes two normalizations instead of one:

- `applyAuditFieldGovernance` (#4513, unchanged): the VALUE half — a DECLARED audit field reports the writability the engine enforces.
- `applyInjectedSystemColumns` (new): the PRESENCE half — an UNDECLARED injected column is added.

Because that seam is already wired into every exit, all of them converge at once: the single-item read, the plural spelling, the list, the cached/ETag branch, both draft reads, and the layered read's `effective` layer.

### The three ruled constraints, one pin each

1. **Injection at the read exits only; `?layers=1`'s `overlay` stays verbatim.** `getMetaItemLayered` already applied `governServedItem` to `effective` and left `code`/`overlay` raw, so this holds by construction. Pinned two ways: the `overlay` layer is asserted `toEqual` the persisted row, and the reverse check below shows the pin actually fires when injection is moved up into that layer.
2. **The write side keeps a strip counterpart.** `saveMetaItem` gained `stripServedSystemColumns` beside the existing `stripReadDecorations` call, same placement and same reason. Kept a separate strip rather than another entry in `METADATA_READ_DECORATIONS`, because the two lists differ in kind: a read decoration is derived diagnostics no schema accepts, whereas an injected column is a real, spec-valid field declaration an author may legitimately write. So the strip removes only a field byte-identical to the platform's own definition — a declared `owner_id` labelled "Responsible Engineer" survives untouched.
3. **`resolveInjectedSystemColumns` (#5378) is the derivation.** Every opt-out row is answered there and re-derived nowhere: `systemFields: false`, `managedBy: 'better-auth'`, `systemFields.audit`/`.tenant`, `tenancy.enabled: false`, the per-tier `ownership` table, the `sys_*` namespace. All seven rows are pinned. `packages/spec` is untouched.

## File surface — declared file by file, because it is wider than the card's

The claim comment scoped this to `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` + tests + one changeset. That scoping presumes the injected-column DEFINITIONS are reachable from the read path. They are not, and this is the measured obstacle:

`resolveInjectedSystemColumns` owns WHICH columns exist (#5378) and deliberately not WHAT each one looks like — that half lived only inside `applySystemFields`, in `@objectstack/objectql`, which **depends on** `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`. The reverse import closes a cycle turbo rejects outright. This is the identical wall #4513 hit and recorded one file over, and the repo has resolved it the same way twice already (`AUDIT_FIELD_GOVERNANCE`, #4513; the write-verb dispatch predicates, #5619): sink the contract into a package both sides already depend on. The alternative — a second definition table inside the read path — is exactly the drift both those relocations exist to prevent.

| file | why |
|:--|:--|
| `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` | the ruled landing: `governServedItem` gains injection; `saveMetaItem` gains the strip |
| `packages/metadata-core/src/injected-system-columns.ts` (new) | the definition table + the `applyInjectedSystemColumns` / `stripInjectedSystemColumns` pair; `metadata-core`'s own deps are `{ @objectstack/spec, zod }`, so no new edge and no new cycle |
| `packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts` | export the module |
| `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` | `applySystemFields` reads the shared table instead of its own literals; the four definitions move out and are re-exported so the symbols still resolve from `@objectstack/objectql`. No behaviour change — objectql's suite passes unchanged |
| `packages/objectql/src/protocol-meta-effective-schema.test.ts` (new) | the core parity pin — see below |
| `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.injected-system-columns.test.ts` (new) | the exits and the three ruled boundaries |
| `.changeset/meta-object-read-effective-schema.md` | user-visible |

**Why the core pin lives in `objectql` and not next to the read path.** The claim is that TWO producers agree, and only that package has both: the real `SchemaRegistry.registerObject` (hence the real `applySystemFields`) and the real protocol read. A pin written in `metadata-protocol` would have to transcribe the registry's answer into a literal and would then be comparing the fix to a copy of itself. There, the registry-backed answer is produced by the engine, live, in both `multiTenant` modes — so the day the table and the injection pass disagree, it fails.

## One key deliberately NOT converged: `organization_id.indexed`

`applySystemFields` stamps `indexed: multiTenant` onto its `organization_id` definition. `indexed` is **not a `FieldSchema` key** — removed in the 16.x line (#2377, ADR-0049) — and `FieldSchema` is `strictObject`, so a document carrying it is rejected by name:

```
Unrecognized key(s) on this field: `indexed`.
  • never a FieldSchema key; a field-level index flag built no index (#2377).
```

Consequence, measured on `origin/main` in both modes: a registry-backed `/meta` object read **already** answers `_diagnostics: { valid: false }` on exactly that key. Its only consumer is `driver-mongodb`'s schema builder, which reads the REGISTERED schema and never a served document.

So the served answer converges on the field SET and on every spec-authorable key, and the DDL hint stays at the injection site. Converging onto a key the object schema refuses would have spread that defect instead of closing this one, and stripping it at the read exit would be a consumer-side patch for a producer-side bug (Prime Directive #12) plus an out-of-scope behaviour change to the registry-backed answer. The residual is pinned in both directions — computed, not enumerated, so a NEW divergence fails by name — and filed separately as objectstack-ai/objectstack#6810.

## Reverse verification — direction predicted first, four runs

| # | change | prediction | result |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | remove injection from `governServedItem` | RED on the new pins; the pre-existing #4326 and #4513 files stay GREEN | 23 of 40 red in the new protocol file; `protocol.read-decorations.test.ts` and `protocol.audit-field-governance.test.ts` both fully green |
| 1b | same, against the cross-package core pin | RED, and the failure text should read as the issue itself | `expected [ 'amount' ] to deeply equal [ 'amount', 'created_at', …(6) ]`; the divergence list goes 1 entry to 50 |
| 2 | keep injection, remove the write-side strip | RED on the NEW round-trip pins **and** on the PRE-EXISTING #4326 pins — that is what proves constraint 2 holds by construction | 6 red, including `protocol.read-decorations.test.ts` "GET → PUT the whole served document stores no _diagnostics" and "keeps the checksum stable" |
| 3 | move injection UP into the `overlay` layer | **inverted** — this pin cannot go red on a revert, since the overlay layer was already verbatim on `origin/main`; its real red direction is a FUTURE change moving injection out of the read exit | both new `?layers=1` pins red, plus #4513's own layered pin |

Run 3 is reported as inverted rather than forced into the usual before-green/after-red shape: removing this PR's change leaves that pin green, so a "revert and watch it go red" line would have been a fabrication. Removals were taken out with `git checkout HEAD -- ...` and each restore verified by an empty `git diff` (never `git stash` — shared stack).

## Tests

- `packages/objectql` — 151 files / 2614 tests, including the 12 new cross-package parity cases (`describe.each([true, false])` over `multiTenant`).
- `packages/metadata-protocol` — 63 files / 740 tests, including 40 new.
- Consumption-radius sweep (a served object document now carries more fields): `@objectstack/rest` 1097, `@objectstack/runtime` 1733, `@objectstack/metadata` 573, `@objectstack/metadata-core` 124, `@objectstack/cli` 1017, `@objectstack/lint` 1652, every `plugin-*` and `service-*` — all green.
- `pnpm build` (71 tasks), `pnpm typecheck` (125 tasks), `pnpm lint`, and both `lint.yml` jobs' gate lists enumerated and run one by one.

Base includes `4bb6f01af` (PR #6779), and `origin/main` is merged in (#6621 landed as #6807 on the `revertCommit` region — disjoint; everything re-verified after the merge, including the new `check:adr-links` gate).
